observation_summary: Calling addDays(0) or other similar date-time addition methods on a MutableDateTime object during a DST transition causes an unexpected change in the object's time value.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by the absence of a check to see if the amount being added is zero. When the amount is zero, the code still proceeds to perform a calculation (setMillis(type.getField(...).add(...))), which, due to the complexities of DST transitions, can result in a different time value even when adding zero. The fix adds a conditional check (if (amount != 0)) to skip the calculation entirely when the addition amount is zero, which is a classic 'Checking' defect type.
evidence_used: The bug report states that addDays(0) changes the value of the object during DST transition.
The fix diff shows that for every 'add' method (addDays, addYears, etc.), a check 'if (amount != 0)' was added to wrap the existing calculation.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix modifies the execution flow, it does not change the underlying algorithm for date addition; it simply adds a guard clause to prevent unnecessary and incorrect execution when the input is zero.
